Telegraph | published 2026-10-01T00:39:00Z | PAYWALLED to curl — content below is Exa snippet quoting the article's own words
headline: Kemi Badenoch to ban young people from signing straight onto benefits if Conservatives win

"Kemi Badenoch will ban young people from signing straight onto benefits if the Conservative Party wins the next election."
"Under plans to be announced at the party's conference, under 25s with fewer than six months of continuous employment would no longer be able to claim universal credit and would instead have to undergo intensive job coaching."
"The policy is part of a fresh welfare crackdown by the Conservative Party, which has already promised to cut £23bn from the benefits bill."
"Under the Tory plans, jobless young people will only be able to claim a new 'Get to Work Allowance' if they take part in a six-month 'Get to Work' programme."
"Those who have not found work or completed the programme would be placed on a subsistence allowance, set at 70 per cent of universal credit, and would be banned from spending the money on alcohol or gambling."
"The Conservatives will unveil a new slogan at their conference, 'Putting the Fair Back into Welfare', in an attempt to draw a clear dividing line between themselves and Mr Burnham, who has said he will not make 'crude cuts' to the benefits bill."
